planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings once frost danger has passed; this selection begins flowering almost immediately after transplanting and needs little coaxing to fill out a mound.

directions: This older, unpatented selection covers itself in single lemon-yellow daisies with a darker gold eye over finely cut medium-green foliage, and it keeps blooming with little deadheading needed. Give it well-drained soil and full sun, and pinch young plants once to encourage the branching mound habit that makes it useful along border edges or as a short seasonal hedge. It tolerates summer heat better than many older marguerite types but still flowers most heavily when nights stay cool.

common_name: Molimba White Marguerite Daisy (Compact White Series Selection)

planting.note: Transplant well-rooted starts after frost risk ends; the tight, well-branched Molimba habit fills containers and hanging baskets quickly without pinching.

directions: Bred for improved branching and heat tolerance over older marguerite lines, Molimba White produces crisp white single daisies with mustard-yellow centers on a naturally compact, self-cleaning plant. It performs well in mixed containers and hanging baskets, holding its shape without regular pinching. Keep the soil evenly moist but never soggy, and feed lightly through the season to sustain continuous bloom from spring until frost.

common_name: Molimba Yellow Marguerite Daisy (Compact Yellow Series Selection)

planting.note: Move transplants outdoors once frost has passed; this compact selection needs no pinching to stay dense and floriferous in beds or containers.

directions: Molimba Yellow carries bright golden-yellow single daisies over dense, finely cut foliage on a mounded plant that resists stretching in warm weather better than older marguerite strains. It suits patio pots, window boxes, and bedding schemes where a tidy, self-branching habit is valued. Water when the top inch of soil dries and avoid letting the roots sit wet, since Argyranthemum resents waterlogged soil.

common_name: Molimba Pink Marguerite Daisy (Compact Pink Series Selection)

planting.note: Plant out after the last frost date into well-drained soil; the compact Molimba habit needs little grooming to stay full and floriferous.

directions: Soft pink single blooms with yellow centers cover this compact, well-branched selection from late spring through the first hard frost. It holds its dense mounded form in containers and beds without the legginess that afflicts older marguerite varieties in summer heat. Deadhead occasionally during peak summer lull to keep fresh buds coming as temperatures moderate in fall.

common_name: Molimba Deep Rose Marguerite Daisy (Compact Dark Pink Series Selection)

planting.note: Set out transplants once nights stay above freezing; this deep-toned selection appreciates the same tight spacing as other Molimba colors for a full, uniform bed.

directions: The deepest-colored member of the Molimba line, this cultivar opens rich rose-pink daisies that read darker than standard Molimba Pink, especially in cool weather. Its compact, self-branching habit keeps plants tidy in mixed containers without pinching. Provide consistent moisture and a mid-season feeding to carry bloom quality through summer heat.

common_name: Grandaisy Bright Yellow Marguerite Daisy (Large-Flowered Yellow Series Selection)

planting.note: Transplant into full sun after frost danger passes; the upright, bushy Grandaisy habit benefits from an early pinch to encourage side branching before flowering ramps up.

directions: Grandaisy Bright Yellow produces unusually large, saturated yellow blooms on an upright, sturdy plant bred to outperform standard marguerite types in flower size and garden impact. It works well as a patio specimen or a bold accent in mixed beds where its bigger flowers can stand out. Deadhead spent blooms to sustain the five-month flowering window from early summer into fall, and keep soil well drained to avoid root rot.

common_name: Grandaisy Deep Red Marguerite Daisy (Large-Flowered Red Series Selection)

planting.note: Set plants out once frost danger has passed; pinch growing tips once at planting to build a fuller framework before the large red blooms take over.

directions: This selection brings a genuinely uncommon deep red tone to the marguerite palette, with oversized daisies held above dark grey-green, finely cut foliage on a sturdy mounding plant. It reads best as a focal point in containers or borders where its unusual color and large flower size can be appreciated up close. Keep it in full sun with even moisture, and expect strong rebloom from early summer through the first fall frosts.

common_name: Comet Pink Marguerite Daisy (Compact Pink Series Selection)

planting.note: Set out transplants after the last frost; the trailing-mounded Comet habit fills window boxes and hanging baskets faster than upright marguerite types.

directions: Comet Pink bears delicate five-petaled pink daisies with a bright yellow eye over a spreading, trailing-mounded plant well suited to hanging baskets and window boxes. Its wide spread relative to its modest height makes it a good spiller alongside more upright annuals in mixed containers. Trim lightly after the first big flush to keep the plant tidy and encourage continued bloom through summer and into fall.

common_name: Comet Yellow Marguerite Daisy (Compact Yellow Series Selection)

planting.note: Transplant after frost danger has passed; this wide-spreading selection is well suited to baskets and window boxes rather than tight bedding rows.

directions: Sharing the low, wide-spreading habit of the Comet series, this yellow-flowered selection produces abundant golden single daisies that cascade nicely over container edges. It flowers most heavily in the cooler weather of late spring and fall, easing off somewhat during peak summer heat. Keep it evenly watered and feed lightly through the season to sustain flower production in hanging displays.

common_name: Comet White Improved Marguerite Daisy (Compact White Series Selection)

planting.note: Move plants outdoors once frost risk has passed; the wide, low-spreading habit performs best where its trailing stems can drape over an edge.

directions: An improved white-flowered selection within the Comet series, this cultivar was refined for cleaner flower color and better garden performance than the original Comet White introduction. Crisp white daisies with yellow centers appear in abundance over a low, broad-spreading plant ideal for baskets and box plantings. Provide full sun and well-drained soil, and pinch back stray stems occasionally to keep the trailing habit balanced.

common_name: Sassy Rose Marguerite Daisy (Compact Rose-Pink Series Selection)

planting.note: Set out after the last frost into full sun; this heat-durable selection tolerates warmer summer stretches better than many older marguerite strains.

directions: Sassy Rose produces large, saturated rose-pink daisies in generous flushes on a compact, durable plant bred for extended heat tolerance compared with standard marguerites. It performs well as a summer-long bedding plant or container specimen in regions where typical Argyranthemum selections stall out in mid-summer warmth. Deadhead periodically to keep bloom count high, and avoid letting the soil dry out completely between waterings.

common_name: Sassy Red Marguerite Daisy (Compact Red Series Selection)

planting.note: Transplant once frost danger has passed; this compact selection holds up well through summer heat where older red-toned marguerites often falter.

directions: One of the few genuinely red-flowered marguerite selections, Sassy Red bears bright red daisies with a contrasting yellow eye on a compact, well-branched plant. It gives beds and containers a warmer color note than the more common white, yellow, and pink Argyranthemum selections. Grow it in full sun with regular moisture, and shear lightly if plants become sparse in the center after the first big bloom flush.

common_name: Sassy White Marguerite Daisy (Compact White Series Selection)

planting.note: Set out transplants after the last frost date; the tight, dwarf habit suits mass plantings and container edges without staking.

directions: Sassy White is a dwarf, tightly compact selection that stays lower and more uniform than most marguerite daisies, making it useful for edging and mass container planting. Clean white flowers with golden eyes appear in heavy flushes from early summer into fall. It thrives in full sun and even moisture, and its naturally tidy habit means it needs little pinching to stay full.

common_name: Vancouver Marguerite Daisy (Classic Double Pink Selection)

planting.note: Transplant into full sun once frost danger has passed; this older, well-established double-flowered cultivar benefits from an early pinch to build a bushier frame.

directions: A long-established favorite, Vancouver produces fully double, quilled pink flowers that give a fuller, softer look than the single-flowered marguerite types. Its woody-based sub-shrub habit builds into a substantial mound over a season, making it a good choice for larger patio containers or as a temporary flowering shrub in mixed borders. Shear it back by about a third if growth becomes loose or leggy, which encourages fresh branching and a new round of bloom.

common_name: Madeira Crested Yellow Marguerite Daisy (Double Quilled Yellow Selection)

planting.note: Set out plants once frost danger has passed; the crested, double flower form of this Madeira series member is a good conversation piece in containers near a patio or entry.

directions: This Madeira series selection stands out for its unusual crested, double yellow flowers with soft creamy overtones, quite different from the flat single daisies of most marguerites. Tiny, finely dissected dark green leaves stay attractive all season on a compact, urban-tolerant plant. Grow it in full sun with consistently moist but not waterlogged soil, and deadhead regularly to keep the distinctive blooms coming from late spring through fall.

common_name: Madeira Cherry Red Marguerite Daisy (Vivid Red Series Selection)

planting.note: Plant out after the last frost date; this fast-establishing Madeira selection reaches full flowering size within a single season and works well as a warm-toned accent among cooler-colored bedding plants.

directions: Madeira Cherry Red brings a rare warm hue to the marguerite lineup, with cherry-red petals surrounding a yellow eye and white center on an upright, mounded plant. Its vigorous, fast-growing habit fills out garden beds, borders, and patio containers quickly and produces flowers that hold up well as cut stems. Trim off faded flower heads regularly to keep new buds forming through summer and into early fall.

common_name: Summer Song White Marguerite Daisy (Double Pompon White Selection)

planting.note: Transplant after frost danger has passed; along mild coastal areas this selection can take full sun, but it appreciates afternoon shade in hotter inland gardens.

directions: Summer Song White produces fully double, pompon-shaped white flowers rather than the flat single daisies typical of most marguerites, giving it a fuller, more textured look in beds and containers. Its main flush runs from spring into early summer, and cutting plants back mid-summer after that flush typically triggers a second round of bloom in autumn. Provide full sun near the coast or light afternoon shade in hot inland climates, along with well-drained soil.
